claude.sample_unit: AI-generated content items (8 diseases x 4 aspects)

links.outcome: Quality scores of ChatGPT content before vs after physician manual revision
links.effect: Physician revision significantly improved understandability (both evaluators p<0.001) and conciseness (p=0.006, p<0.001); scientificity improved significantly only for evaluator 2 (p<0.001); recency, comprehensiveness, interest not significantly changed.
links.quote: In this study, a manual review process was introduced for the content generated by ChatGPT 4.0, and the results showed that manual revision could significantly improve the understandability and conciseness of the content.

links.outcome: Inaccurate, outdated or oversimplified clinical knowledge in ChatGPT content
links.effect: Evaluators found 54 unreasonable contents, including 25 inaccurate knowledge (11 errors, 6 outdated knowledge, 8 overly simple descriptions) and 29 unclear logic.
links.quote: Two evaluators evaluated the content of ChatGPT 4.0 and found 54 unreasonable contents, including inaccurate knowledge (25 in total, 11 of errors, 6 of outdated knowledge, 8 of overly simple description) and unclear logic (29 in total, 13 of repeated content, 16 of inconsistent content with the topic) ( Table 2 ).

links.outcome: Understandability, conciseness and interest ratings of AI-generated patient education content
links.effect: Understandability, conciseness and interest scored lower than scientificity, recency and comprehensiveness (ANOVA across dimensions p<0.001; e.g., evaluator 1 understandability 15.00 and interest 11.25 vs comprehensiveness 18.25).
links.quote: Compared with scientificity, recency and comprehensiveness, the scores of understandability, conciseness, and interest were significantly reduced.

links.outcome: physician review caught AI content problems
links.effect: Physician review found 54 unreasonable contents: 25 inaccurate knowledge (11 errors, 6 outdated, 8 overly simple) and 29 unclear logic.
links.quote: Two evaluators evaluated the content of ChatGPT 4.0 and found 54 unreasonable contents, including inaccurate knowledge (25 in total, 11 of errors, 6 of outdated knowledge, 8 of overly simple description) and unclear logic (29 in total, 13 of repeated content, 16 of inconsistent content with the topic) ( Table 2 ).

links.outcome: understandability and conciseness of patient education
links.effect: Baseline understandability 15.00±1.07/13.25±1.28, conciseness 15.13±1.73/13.88±1.46, interest 11.25±0.71/9.88±1.36; dimension differences P<0.001.
links.quote: Compared with scientificity, recency and comprehensiveness, the scores of understandability, conciseness, and interest were significantly reduced.

links.outcome: inaccurate or unreasonable generated medical content
links.effect: 54 unreasonable contents: 25 inaccurate knowledge and 29 unclear logic; inaccurate knowledge included 11 errors, 6 outdated knowledge, 8 overly simple descriptions.
links.quote: Two evaluators evaluated the content of ChatGPT 4.0 and found 54 unreasonable contents, including inaccurate knowledge (25 in total, 11 of errors, 6 of outdated knowledge, 8 of overly simple description) and unclear logic (29 in total, 13 of repeated content, 16 of inconsistent content with the topic) ( Table 2 ).

links.outcome: understandability of generated urological disease popularization content
links.effect: Understandability scored significantly lower than comprehensiveness and recency across diseases (evaluator 1: 15.00±1.07 vs 18.25±0.89 and 17.25±0.89; evaluator 2: 13.25±1.28 vs 18.38±0.92 and 16.63±1.30; both P<0.001)
links.quote: ChatGPT 4.0 generated content scored high in scientificity, recency, and comprehensiveness, while scoring relatively low in understandability, conciseness, and interest.
